qa.reply:
Yes
From the QA lens, this rule is testable red-first and prevents unobserved bad state. Audit checks can mechanically verify the takeover sequence: any takeover lacking a prior stop record in rulings fails red first. Briefing lock-waiting seats to run in the foreground and explicitly stopping them by task or process ID prevents lingering background watchers from leaking concurrent execution into worktrees. Note: card rulings should record verified process termination to ensure audit checks detect any failure to release lock resources.

CITE: Stop a waiting seat before its runs are taken over
